Programmable physical keys are fast becoming a core element of advanced user workflows, including agentic programming. Logitech is now officially bringing a compact, desk-friendly option to market.

Logitech today announced the MX Keypad, a $99.99 accessory featuring nine customisable full-colour LCD keys for launching commands, executing macros and connecting to AI tools.

The MX Keypad costs half the price of the Logitech MX Creative Console

If the hardware looks familiar, that's no coincidence. The Logitech MX Creative Console pairs an LCD keypad with a separate dial pad for tweaking settings and controlling creative apps.

The MX Keypad offers a pure keypad experience without the extra controller, priced at half the Creative Console's $199.99 MSRP.

The new product is pitched primarily at developer and AI workflows, but its customisation isn't limited to coding apps.

The Logi Options+ app lets you tailor the experience

Through the free Logi Options+ app, users can assign hotkeys, saved prompts, scripts and macros to individual keys. Two paging buttons can switch between up to 15 pages, while app-aware profiles automatically change layouts when you switch applications.

This means the same row of physical keys can serve different functions in VS Code, Slack, Chrome or other apps. The Logi Marketplace offers plugins, profiles and icon packs, and a built-in icon editor lets users design the look of each key themselves.

You can use AI to set up your AI keypad

When I first sat down to try it out, I connected the MX Keypad to my MacBook Air on the desk and asked Codex, using computer use, to help me programme custom keys in Logi Options+ based on how I use ChatGPT on my Mac.

Asking an AI coding agent to help you configure physical keys you'll use to operate AI is itself a neat twist, and it neatly illustrates the appeal: putting the prompts and actions you tap out all the time onto dedicated, labelled keys.

The MX Keypad is a product of Logitech's collaboration with GitHub. It ships with built-in GitHub Copilot integration for VS Code, and both new and existing users can redeem three months of Copilot Pro+ free through Logi Options+.

The MX Keypad supports community plugins

Logitech also noted that community-built plugins for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex offer agent status tracking, terminal control and more. Developers wanting to go further can build their own plugins using the Logi Actions SDK, which supports C# and Node.js.

The keypad connects via USB-C and runs on macOS 13 or later and Windows 10 or later. It measures roughly 3.6 x 3.1 inches and weighs 96 grams, taking up little room next to a laptop or keyboard.

The MX Keypad goes on sale today (8 September) in Graphite and Pale Grey, priced at $99.99.
